waterbodyIdentityDecision: Retain the publication’s Marikina River system and four named sampling communities as a dated research crosswalk to the prior NCR lead. This review does not establish a canonical waterbody identity, river geometry, or a new region assignment.
question: Does the 2026 PJSB full article add site-specific host-fish counts to the 2023 Marikina parasite-study preprint, and can those counts be treated as independent or current fish records?

source.citation: To, D. A. L., Gomez, G. M. L., Pavia, R. T. B., Jr., Choudhury, A., & Briones, J. C. A. (2026). First report on the parasitic fauna of invasive alien fish species in Marikina River system, Philippines. Philippine Journal of Systematic Biology, 19(1), 19–27. https://doi.org/10.26757/pjsb202519005
source.license: CC BY-NC 3.0 under the PJSB Open Access Policy
source.licenseNote: The journal policy states that PJSB articles are distributed under CC BY-NC 3.0. This permits non-commercial reuse with attribution, not unrestricted commercial use. No article images or figure crops are reproduced in this review.

relationshipToPriorStudy.assessment: The 2026 article has the same five authors as the 2023 preprint, reports the same 187 fish, eight fish taxa, four named communities and coordinates, and the same July/October 2021 and January/February 2022 study collection period. It appears to report the same underlying collection dataset in its formal journal publication; treat the two documents as related versions of one study, not independent corroboration.
relationshipToPriorStudy.inferenceBoundary: The exact match in authorship, sample total, taxa, localities, coordinates, and collection period supports this relationship assessment. The article does not explicitly state in the reviewed text that it is a revised version of the Research Square preprint.

methodReview.studyPurpose: Document invasive alien fish hosts collected in the Marikina River system and examine their endoparasites.
methodReview.designAndGear: The article says host fish were collected from river littoral areas with local fishermen using drift gill nets, beach seines, hand nets, fish traps, and fishing rods.
methodReview.dateLimitation: These are study collection months; the article does not assign individual capture dates or months to each fish or taxon.
methodReview.siteCoordinatesDisposition: The four coordinates in the article match the coordinates already recorded in the prior 2023 crosswalk at the source-reported precision. They identify study sites, not specimen-level locations; no geometry or app coordinates are added.
methodReview.identificationMethod: The article reports fish identification using taxonomic keys and online databases including FishBase. No voucher catalogue numbers or specimen repository were located in the reviewed full text; the source identifications are not independently re-examined here.
methodReview.sampleCountMeaning: Table 1 counts are fish collected for a parasite-host study. They are not population abundance, fishery catch, catch-per-unit-effort, or a complete community inventory.

taxonomyAndIdentity.priorChecklist: COL26.10 XR name cross-checks recorded in the linked 2023 crosswalk.
taxonomyAndIdentity.interpretation: All eight table names are already present in the prior crosswalk. Existing checklist matches are nomenclatural only; they do not independently verify the specimens, localities, native/introduced status, or current presence. No new taxonomy match or fish taxon is added by this review.

imageReview.figure: Figure 2, printed page 21 of the PDF
imageReview.visualFinding: All eight fish photographs are caption-labeled and show a 5 cm scale bar. The panels are clear side views. Their captions agree with Table 1 names, but are source-reported identifications rather than independent voucher re-identifications.
imageReview.rightsAndDisposition: The article falls under the journal’s CC BY-NC 3.0 policy. No panel was cropped, copied, or added to src/lib/species-images.ts because the license is non-commercial-only and Bangwit’s future commercial compatibility is not established. Retain the figure as cited research evidence only.

scopeAndReuseDecision.decision: Research-only dated study crosswalk; no public species projection or app image admission.
scopeAndReuseDecision.reason: The journal publication strengthens the source status and supplies site-specific sample counts, but it appears to use the same 2021–2022 cohort as the 2023 preprint. The parasite-study sample is not a complete fish survey; per-taxon dates and specimen-level coordinates are absent, vouchers were not located, and the image license is non-commercial-only.

nonClaims: The 187 fish are a study sample, not the Marikina River population size or fishery catch.
The site-level counts do not provide per-fish dates, specimen-level GPS, validated river geometry, or a current occurrence estimate.
The eight host taxa are not a complete Marikina River fish checklist; taxa not listed are not absent.
The paper frames the sampled fish as invasive alien fish; this review does not independently establish each taxon’s national origin or invasive status.
The 2023 preprint and 2026 journal article are likely versions of one study, not independent confirmation.
Parasite-host findings do not establish human health effects, fish edibility, food safety, diet, bait, catchability, or fishing rules.
Captioned fish photos are not independently verified app reference images and are not copied into the image registry.
nextActions: Retain the full article and preprint as one related Marikina host-fish study with separate source and reuse records.
For future occurrence admission, seek specimen/voucher identifiers or independent, date-resolved fish observations and validate locality precision.
Continue NCR source and waterbody coverage work; NCR and all Luzon regional baselines remain incomplete.
Keep the figure out of the species-image registry unless Bangwit’s intended use is non-commercial and the per-image admission checklist is satisfied.
